note: RIGHTS (register applied, not re-derived): instrument_rights_register.csv carries a settled RFQ row, verdict ship_with_note, ruled by Ben on 2026-09-10 on this very table's batch_163 escalation. The caution that must travel with the wording, quoted from the rights holders' page (UCL Psychoanalysis Unit, Fonagy & Luyten; Internet Archive snapshot 20260308175751, sha256 97a728a9...): "The RFQ is freely available to download for research purposes. The measure is not yet suited for clinical purposes." and "If you are interested in translating the RFQ, or if you have any other questions, please contact us." Why it does not block: the second sentence disclaims fitness (clinical use) and reserves nothing, which is the LOT-R shape (2026-09-08); per Ben's 2026-09-10 ruling the first sentence describes a free download offer with no 'only', fee, permission requirement, NC/ND term or redistribution bar, and the 'contact us' is scoped to making a translation, not to using or redistributing one. The Spanish version shipped here is the study's published translation, not one IRW made. CODE DERIVATION: pattern 1 -- data/ruiz_parra_2023_rfq_battery.py selects columns whose names start with 'RFQ8' from the S9 sheet 'Spanish RFQ non-clinical' and melts them by name, so the IRW item code IS the header (RFQ8_1..RFQ8_8, header row 1). But the header carries only a number and the workbook has no labels, so the tie from number to wording comes from the paper's appendices, which number the items 1-8: mapping_basis=paper_explicit, and Step 5b was run rather than exempted. S1 (English) and S2 (Spanish) numberings correspond item for item by content (1 thoughts of others a mystery; 2 not always know why I do what I do; 3 angry, say things without knowing why; 4 angry, say things I regret; 5 insecure, behave in ways that bother others; 6 do things without knowing why; 7 always know what I feel; 8 strong feelings cloud thinking). STEP 3b: live table is the RFQ-8 (8 items, resp 1-7) and not one of the eight sibling scales in the same sheet. TRANSCRIPTION: Spanish item_text, the two end anchors and the instructions are verbatim from S2 (PDF text layer, no OCR); item stems wrapped across lines in the PDF table and were joined with a single space. English items verbatim from S1 including its curly apostrophes, with ONE normalisation: S1 prints item 8 as 'Strong feelings often cloud my thinking .' with a space before the full stop, removed here. S2 labels only the scale ends ('Muy en desacuerdo' at 1, 'Muy de acuerdo' at 7); option_text for resp 2-6 is blank, not padded. The instructions describe 4 as the neutral/undecided midpoint, but it carries no label on the scale, so that text stays in instructions and option_text for 4 stays blank. TRANSLATIONS (translation_source=mixed): item_text_translated and option_text_translated are the English original RFQ as printed in this study's S1 Appendix -- a parallel version, not a back-translation of the Spanish strings; S1's anchors are 'Strongly disagree'/'Strongly agree'. instructions_translated is IRW's own translation of the Spanish S2 instructions, because S1's English instructions are a different text ('Please work through the next 8 statements... write it beside the statement. Do not think too much about it') and would misrepresent what these respondents read; that project-generated English is disclosed in public_note. KEYING: item 7 is the RFQ-8's only positively-worded item and is reverse-scored in the paper's unidimensional scoring; the live table stores it RAW (it is the only item correlating negatively with all 7 others). resp is the as-administered 1-7 agreement. DATA: live 605 respondents vs the paper's 602; items 4,5,6,8 have 604 rows. The processing script dropped one -9 in RFQ8_4 as a data-entry error. Every item uses all 7 levels. STEP 5b: PARTIAL -- see verification_ruiz_parra_2023_rfq8.csv; every item is pinned except that the order within the near-collinear pair 3/4 is only weakly favoured.
public_note: The English instructions (instructions_translated) were translated by IRW from the Spanish; the English item and anchor wording is the original English RFQ printed in the study's S1 Appendix, a parallel version rather than a translation of the Spanish items; item 7 ('Siempre sé lo que siento') is stored unreversed.

note: (1) IDENTITY / Step 3b: the postprint never mentions a tightness measure (0 hits for tight|loose|Gelfand in its text; Supplementary Tables SM10/SM11 omit it too), and the analysis script never scores Tight*. Identity was established through the administering project instead: the postprint says Study 3 was collected in the second wave of the International Situations Project (ISP), and the ISP's own 'Translated Measures' component lists exactly the Study 3 CSV's column families (BFI-2, HEXACO honesty, IHS, LOT-R, MicroMacro Environment, NARQ, Religiosity, Risk, Self-construal, SHS, Tightness-looseness, Trustworthiness). Its 'Tightness Looseness Scale (Spanish).docx' is a 6-item Gelfand et al. (2011) scale translated by this paper's own authors Gallardo-Pujol and Oceja; Kuper et al. (JPSP, ISP) describe the same measure as '6-item ... (5-point rating scale) of cultural tightness'. Live table: 6 items, resp 1-5 -- consistent. So instrument = Gelfand et al. (2011) Tightness/Looseness Scale, 5-point ISP administration (Gelfand's original used 6 points; not carried over). (2) TEXT: text_source=study_materials -- the ISP survey IS the administration this study's data came from, one hop off the kp572 deposit via the postprint's own statement; flagged here because it is not a file in the deposit itself. item_text/instructions/option_text are the Spanish survey page screenshots (Spanish ISP.pdf pp. 28-29), transcribed by eye from an image-only PDF (no text layer; OCR-equivalent -- spot-check). The survey's question number '9. ' was stripped from instructions. Transcribed literally including the source typo 'les personas' (for 'las personas') in item 4; the survey screenshot reads 'amplia' where the translation docx reads 'ámplia' and the docx items lack final periods -- the screenshot, being what respondents saw, was used. _translated fields = the ISP English survey (English ISP.pdf p. 22), translation_source=study_supplied; it matches Gelfand's canonical wording, whereas the ISP docx English column drops 'that' (item 1) and 'deciding' (item 4) -- the survey version was used. Caveat: the website PDFs are undated screenshots; that they show the exact wave-2 build is assumed, not proven. (3) MAPPING: Tight1..Tight6 are the source CSV's own column names but carry no text; tied to wording by survey display order (paper_order). Verification PARTIAL (verify_ script): live table tied to OSF file (6/6 n=419, means 3.88/3.94/3.33/2.91/3.67/2.80); Tight4 is the unique item behaving as reverse-worded, as Gelfand item 4 ('freedom') is -- only reversal raising alpha (.408 -> .436; others -.095..+.222), only negative mean inter-item r (-.019 vs +.101..+.190), only negative PC1 loading (-.13). Weak signal, stated honestly. Direction: same export stores the identically formatted, all-positive IHS so that it reproduces the published M 3.49/SD .54 (3.488/.541; reversed 2.512), and LOT likewise (batch_165) -- so 1 = Totalmente en desacuerdo. Display-order preservation corroborated on sibling scales: authors' keys for Constru1-4/5-9/10-13 and LOT1-6 follow the ISP website order and 6/6, 10/10, 6/6, 15/15 correlations carry the predicted sign. NOT established: order among Tight1,2,3,5,6. (4) RIGHTS: no register row for this instrument; none written. No restriction located: the ISP translation docx and survey pages carry only the NSF acknowledgement; stressmeasurement.org/tightloose states no permission/licence/fee terms; no originator (Gelfand) terms page found. ISP OSF project yv2nq states no licence. Silence is permission -> extracted normally. Not a ship verdict for the register. (5) Every item uses all five resp levels. correct_response empty (attitude scale).
public_note: The item codes Tight1-Tight6 are matched to wording by the order the International Situations Project survey displayed the items; the data confirm that Tight4 is the reverse-worded 'freedom' item but cannot confirm the order of the other five, and item 4's Spanish reproduces the survey's own typo 'les personas'.

Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv RFQ row (ship_with_note, 2026-09-10).
note: Administered in Serbian (paper: questionnaire presented 'in Serbian'; 'the Serbian version of the RFQ-8'), so language=Serbian; ships English in the base fields as a translated_substitute with the _translated columns empty. RECOVERABILITY CHECKED, scoped to deposit + paper supplements: the article has exactly one supplement, S1 Data (.sav); its RFQ1..RFQ8 columns carry NO variable labels (all NULL, read with pyreadstat) and their value labels are English ('Strongly disagree','I disagree','I partially disagree','I neither agree nor disagree','I partially agree','I agree','Strongly agree'), so there is zero Serbian item wording in scope. The paper quotes only two items, in the authors' own English paraphrase ('Human thoughts are a mystery to me', 'Sometimes I do things without actually knowing why'); those paraphrases were NOT used. The rights holder's RFQ page (Internet Archive snapshot 20260308175751, sha256 f63c42cc...) lists no Serbian version, and its 'English version' zip is not archived (Wayback returns an HTML stub), so the official English form could not be opened. translation_source=mixed: item_text is third_party_english -- transcribed from Horvath et al. 2023 Table 2 with the authors' '(reversed)' annotation on item 7 dropped and typographic apostrophes written as ASCII; it matches the Ruiz-Parra 2023 S1 Appendix English form word for word, differing only in that form's terminal periods (kept off, matching Horvath and the shipped rfq_wozniakprus_2021); option_text is study_supplied -- the .sav's own English value labels, all 7 points labelled, identical for all 8 items, and exactly the label->number map in data/safiye_2023_mbi_rfq.py (MAP_RFQ). instructions left blank: the study publishes none, and the canonical form's instructions ('choose a number ... and write it beside the statement', endpoint-only anchors) describe a paper form, not this study's online administration with seven labelled points. MAPPING: codes RFQ1..RFQ8 are the .sav column names (pattern 1, no rename), but with no variable labels the name->wording tie is the instrument's published numbering, hence paper_order; checked in verify_safiye_2023_rfq.R (VERDICT: PASS), PARTIAL because RFQ2 vs RFQ6 is not separable. RFQ7 ('I always know what I feel') is the reverse-keyed item and is stored RAW in the live table (negative r with all 7 other items). RIGHTS: register row applied, not re-derived -- ship_with_note. Quoted from the rights holder (UCL Psychoanalysis Unit, archived page above): 'The RFQ is freely available to download for research purposes. The measure is not yet suited for clinical purposes.' The second sentence disclaims fitness and does not block (LOT-R rule, 2026-09-08); the first reserves no right (no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution term; the page's 'please contact us' is scoped to translating the RFQ), per Ben's 2026-09-10 ruling recorded in the register. No response-data defect found: live per-item value counts equal the deposit's in all 56 cells.
public_note: The RFQ-8 was administered to this sample in Serbian, but neither the study's data deposit nor its paper contains the Serbian item wording, so the item text shipped here is the standard English RFQ-8 wording standing in for what respondents read; the response labels are the study's own English labels from its data file. Item RFQ7 ("I always know what I feel") is reverse-keyed and is stored unreversed. The instrument's authors note the RFQ is not yet suited for clinical purposes.
